questions.question: Which late veteran tribal leader of Tripura received the Padma Shri posthumously in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Narendra Chandra Debbarma.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Narendra Chandra Debbarma was recognized for his contributions to the **tribal community **and his significant efforts in promoting the welfare and rights of the indigenous populations in Tripura.
 
• He was known for his deep commitment to preserving the **cultural heritage **and traditions of the tribal communities in Tripura.
 
• He worked extensively to promote indigenous art, music, and dance forms, ensuring that they received recognition and appreciation both locally and nationally.
 
• Debbarma was also involved in **political activism**, advocating for the rights of tribal people within the legislative framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sindhu Chandra Jamatia** was instrumental in preserving the traditional customs of the Jamatia tribe and worked on improving the welfare of tribal communities in Tripura.
 
• **Bhaba Ranjan Reang **was known for his efforts in popularizing Reang tribal music and worked to safeguard his community’s cultural heritage.
 
• **Araber Rahaman **focused on enhancing educational opportunities in rural areas and played a crucial role in advocating for social development among underprivileged communities.

questions.question: In which of the following years, NABARD sanctions Action Research Project to MYRADA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1987**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• MYRADA, an **NGO based in Karnataka**, was involved in helping resettle landless laborers and rural poor.
 
• Through this project, NABARD and MYRADA experimented with the concept of Self-Help Groups (SHGs), which evolved into a significant **microfinance **movement in India.
 
• The aim of the Action Research Project was to assess how informal groups, primarily consisting of women, could self-manage resources, promote savings, and provide loans to group members.
 
• This initiative led to the creation of a system where rural communities, especially women, were empowered to control financial activities, leading to better financial inclusion.
 
• The success of the project encouraged NABARD to replicate and promote the SHG model across India, making it a vital component of rural credit structures and one of the largest microfinance programs in the world.

questions.question: Which of the following is the reason for unemployment?

options.text: Large migration to a particular area

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Large migration to a particular area**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Large Migration to a Particular Area: **Large-scale migration can lead to an oversupply of labor in certain areas, especially if the job market cannot absorb the influx of workers. This can result in increased competition for available jobs and **higher unemployment **rates among newcomers. Hence** option 2 is correct**. 
 
• **Slow Population Growth: **It can lead to fewer new job seekers entering the labor market. This could potentially stabilize or **reduce unemployment **if the economy can sustain job creation at a level that meets the needs of the existing population.
 
• **Good Education System **typically **reduces unemployment **by equipping individuals with the necessary skills for the job market.
 
• **Fast Economic Growth **usually leads to increased job creation, thereby **lowering unemployment **rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Types of unemployment:**

__
 
• **Frictional **Unemployment: This occurs when individuals are temporarily without a job while transitioning from one position to another or entering the workforce for the first time.
 
• **Structural **Unemployment: This happens when there is a mismatch between the skills of the workforce and the skills needed for available jobs, often due to technological advancements or shifts in the economy.
 
• **Cyclical **Unemployment: This type is related to the economic cycle, where unemployment rises during economic downturns and falls during periods of economic growth.
 
• **Seasonal **Unemployment: Occurs in industries that experience fluctuations in demand at certain times of the year, such as agriculture or tourism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global **Unemployment Rate: According to the International Labour Organization (ILO), the global unemployment rate in 2023 is estimated to be around 5.8%. 
 
• In **India**, the unemployment rate as of 2024 is estimated to be around 7.7%, according to various surveys and reports. The rate varies significantly by region and demographics .

questions.question: In Himachal Pradesh, which of the following is a floral festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Phulaich festival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Himachal Pradesh, the floral festival is the** Phulaich festival.**
 
• This festival, also known as the **Ookayand or Ukyam,** is celebrated in the **Kinnaur district.**
 
• The festival is celebrated every September, coinciding with the 16th day of the Hindu calendar month of **Bhadrapada.**
 
• It is celebrated in honor of the local deity and is a time when the local communities pay **tribute to their ancestors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baisakhi **is celebrated on **April 13th every year.** Sometimes, it falls on April 14th.
 
• Traditionally, Baisakhi is a spring **harvest festival in Punjab**, celebrating the first harvesting of the crops for the year.
 
• **For Sikhs**, **Baisakhi marks the Sikh New Year** and is one of the most significant dates in the Sikh calendar.
 
• **The Chaitraul Festival, **celebrated in the** Sirmaur area of Himachal Pradesh**, is a culturally rich event.
 
• The Chaitraul Festival is celebrated in the **month of Chaitra,** which typically falls between March and April in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• **The Doongri Festival** is a vibrant and culturally rich event celebrated in **Himachal Pradesh.** 
 
• The Doongri Festival is primarily celebrated in the** Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh,** specifically in the town of Manali, within the sacred Dhungri Forest.

questions.question: What was the primary purpose of the "Intensive Agricultural District Program (IADP)" launched during the Green Revolution in India?

options.text: Increasing agricultural productivity in specific districts
Boosting the cultivation of cash crops

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Increasing agricultural productivity in specific districts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Intensive Agricultural District Program (IADP)** was** launched in 1960-61** in India.
 
• It focused on the intensive use of inputs such as high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and modern irrigation techniques.
 
• The program primarily focused on **wheat, rice, maize, and millet,** which were considered staple food grains in India.
 
• The IADP was launched by the Ministry of Agriculture during the **tenure of Jawaharlal Nehru as PM**. At the time, the **Agriculture Minister was S. K. Patil.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Initially, the program was introduced in 7 districts across various states that had high potential for agricultural production.
 
• These districts included: **West Godavari (Andhra Pradesh), Shahabad (Bihar), Raipur (Madhya Pradesh), Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu), Ludhiana (Punjab), Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh), and Pali (Rajasthan).**
 
• The** Green Revolution refers** to a period of significant agricultural transformation in India **during the 1960s and 1970s.**
 
• **In India**, **M. S. Swaminathan** is known as the **Father of the Green Revolution** for introducing these scientific agricultural practices to India.
 
• **Globally, Dr. Norman Borlaug**, an American agronomist, is regarded as the **father of the Green Revolution **for his pioneering work in developing high-yielding wheat varieties.
 
• The Green Revolution began in 1965, during the tenure of Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, and continued into the early 1970s.
 
• The Green Revolution was **most successful in the Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh**, where the required infrastructure, such as irrigation, was already well-developed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the SI unit of temperature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Kelvin__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The kelvin is the** base unit of temperature **in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The zero point of the kelvin scale is absolute zero, **defined as 0 K. **This **corresponds to -273.15°C or -459.67°F.**
 
• To convert from Celsius to Kelvin, you add 273.15.** For example, 25°C is equivalent to 298.15 K.**
 
• The unit is named after **William Thomson**, 1st Baron Kelvin, who made significant contributions to thermodynamics and the understanding of temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Room temperature** is typically around **293 K (20°C or 68°F).**
 
• **The pascal is** the SI unit of pressure, defined as one **newton per square meter (N/m²).**
 
• The unit **Pascal** is named after **Blaise Pascal,** a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.
 
• The **Fahrenheit **scale is a temperature scale used primarily in the United States, where **water freezes at 32°F and boils at 212°F.**
 
• The **Celsius scale **is a temperature scale used worldwide, where water** freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C.**
 
• The Celsius scale is **named after Anders Celsius**, a Swedish astronomer who developed the scale in **1742.**

questions.question: Proposed by Lord Lytton, then viceroy of India (governed 1876 - 80), the act was intended to prevent the vernacular press from expressing criticism of British policies-notably, the opposition that had grown with the outset of the Second _________ (1878 - 80).
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Anglo-Afghan War.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • Lord Lytton was the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880. • The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was enacted to** curb the freedom of the Indian-language press.** • The act was a response to the growing criticism of British policies, especially during the Second **Anglo-Afghan War (1878-1880).** • The act allowed the government to confiscate the printing press, paper, and other materials of a newspaper if it published seditious material. • **Amrita Bazar Patrika, **this prominent Bengali newspaper **converted itself into an English-language** publication overnight to circumvent the restrictions imposed by the Vernacular Press Act. • **Hindoo Patriot,** another significant newspaper, the Hindoo Patriot, chose to** stop its operations** rather than comply with the act’s stringent regulations.

questions.question: Complete the sentence. "Most of Ashoka's inscriptions __________."

options.text: were in Prakrit and were written in the Brahmi script
were in Brahmi and were written in the Prakrit script
were in Sanskrit and were written in the Brahmi script
were in Prakrit and were written in the Devnagri script

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**were in Prakrit and were written in the Brahmi script.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Most of Ashoka’s inscriptions were written in Prakrit**, which was the common language of the people during his reign.
 
• The inscriptions were primarily written in the **Brahmi script**, which is one of the oldest writing systems used in India.
 
• These inscriptions were used to spread **Ashoka’s messages of Dhamma (moral law) and to communicate with his subjects.**
 
• Ashoka’s inscriptions are found across the Indian subcontinent, indicating the vast extent of his empire and his efforts to communicate with a diverse population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some of Ashoka’s inscriptions were also written in **Greek and Aramaic,** especially in the northwestern parts of his empire.
 
• The inscriptions were deciphered by **James Prinsep in the 19th century,** which was a significant breakthrough in understanding ancient Indian history.
 
• Besides Brahmi, the** Kharosthi script** was also used in some regions.
 
• These inscriptions provide valuable insights into the **administrative practices, social policies, and religious beliefs during Ashoka’s reign.**
